newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire acknowledges panic in rebel-threatened town.
newsitem.headline: Zaire acknowledges panic in rebel-threatened town.

text.p: Zaire said on Tuesday panic had swept through Kindu but added its forces still controlled the eastern town, a major base for army operations identified by rebels as their next target.
A senior defence ministry official told Reuters that panic grew worse on Monday on news that the governor was trying to leave town by plane -- on a trip that was already planned.
But he said his information suggested rebels had not advanced beyond Kalima, 80 km (50 miles) further east.
A senior official of state rail network CIZARAIL, in contact with Kindu, said that residents had fled into the surrounding forest, fearing a rebel attack.
But both officials denied reports of looting by soldiers in the town, which is capital of Maniema province and a mining and transport hub.
Defence ministry officials said panic set in after Rwandan refugees fleeing rebel advances further east arrived in Kindu.
"The governor was trying to leave town by plane yesterday. The fact that local authorities were trying to leave helped to provoke the panic," the defence ministry official said.
"People believed that if the governor was leaving he must have information suggesting the rebels are close," he added.
The rebels took up arms in October and have since captured towns and territory in the east. They blunted a January 20 government counter-offensive with attacks on several fronts.
Rebel leader Laurent Kabila, in South Africa for talks on the war, has threatened a major rebel offensive if ailing and veteran President Mobutu Sese Seko does not start negotiations.
